newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's GMD wins water projects.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's GMD wins water projects.

text.p: Mexican construction firm Grupo Mexicano de Desarrollo SA de CV (GMD) said on Tuesday it had been awarded public works projects worth 306 million pesos in the Caribbean state of Quintana Roo.
"GMD will invest 306 million pesos over three years in Quintana Roo (state) to set up hydraulic infrastructure and drainage," the company said in a news release.

The project is being paid for by the International Finance Corporation, an affiliate of the World Bank, and Mexico's state-run public works bank Banco Nacional de Obras y Servicios Publicos (Banobras), the release said.
GMD said its subsidiaries Hidraulicos de Cancun SA de CV and Aguakan SA de CV will invest 72 million pesos on the first phase of the project this year.
The National Water Commission and the Quintana Roo Housing Institute also will participate in the project, GMD said.
